title: Value Record — frontmatter
description: Schema for the YAML frontmatter of a Value Record (VR), per spec-value-record.md v2.0.0 §4.2. The record is the governed memory of an Operational Value Commitment. It validates the machine-readable fields only; the markdown body is human judgement and is deliberately not schema-constrained. Note the two independent state axes: `status` is epistemic, `realisation` is about the value. Adopter-specific fields are permitted under the `x-` namespace, as for the TDR. This schema validates v2 records; v1 records remain valid v1 records and are not validated here. See TDR-0008, TDR-0019.

^x-.description: Adopter extension namespace. Name extensions `x-<owner>-<field>` to avoid collision. The standard defines no meaning for these fields, no expectation of portability, and schema validity implies nothing about security.

id.description: VR-nnnn, unique within the owning organisation or repository.

title.description: Declarative statement of what is being pursued or preserved.

status.description: The EPISTEMIC state — what is known about the record. Independent of `realisation`. A candidate has no organisational standing whether drafted by a person or assembled from evidence.

realisation.description: The VALUE state — what is known about the value. `attribution-unresolved` (outcome observed, attribution not evidenced) is a legitimate settlement, not an incomplete one.

linked_decisions.description: One or more TDR ids. Never `none` — a value claim floating free of any decision is a forecast, not a record.

beneficiary.description: Whose outcome is being pursued or preserved. IDENTITY-BEARING, not descriptive metadata: two commitments identical in every other respect but differing in beneficiary are two commitments (spec-value-record.md §4.3).

committed_by.description: A named individual who commits the organisation — not a committee, not a role.

authority.description: The authority under which the organisation is bound — a mandate, delegation, board approval or governing decision, traceable to something.

finance_countersignatory.description: A named individual in the finance function — not a committee, not a role. Co-signs at ratification, every material state change, and any write-off. Required for the transition to `ratified`, not for the record to exist: a candidate may legitimately lack one (specification §4.4), and encoding a transition requirement as an unconditional structural one would collapse structural validity into lifecycle-transition eligibility. See TDR-0039.

reconcile_by.description: ISO 8601 date, YYYY-MM-DD. Frontmatter is validated as JSON: normalise YAML native dates to ISO-8601 strings before validation.

vrRefList.description: One or more VR ids (comma-separated), or the literal `none`.

then.description: A record may lack a baseline or counter-signatory only while `candidate`. Fields checkable here are already required; the baseline is a body section and is checked by the admission test, not the schema.

realisation.description: A candidate has no organisational standing, so its value cannot yet be observing, realised or settled.
